vocabulary.meaning_en: to start working seriously on something
vocabulary.example: OK, everyone, let's get down to business.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to tell people about a job, product or event, e.g. online or in a newspaper
vocabulary.note_ar: الاسم advertisement، ويُختصر advert (بريطاني) أو ad.
vocabulary.note_en: Noun: advertisement (UK short: advert; also ad).
vocabulary.example: We'll advertise the job online.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person or thing that takes the place of another
vocabulary.example: We need a replacement for Tom.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to change things
vocabulary.example: The new manager wants to make some changes in the office.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to make a business successful again after a difficult time
vocabulary.meaning_ar: يُنهض بالشركة من جديد؛ يقلب وضعها
vocabulary.example: She turned the business round in just two years.

vocabulary.meaning_en: wanting very much to do something
vocabulary.example: I'm keen to hear your ideas.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to come together around someone
vocabulary.example: Could we all gather round for a quick meeting?

vocabulary.meaning_en: a short meeting
vocabulary.example: Let's have a quick meeting before lunch.

vocabulary.meaning_en: very useful or important
vocabulary.example: He was a valuable member of the team.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to take action to solve a problem
vocabulary.example: As the boss, you must deal with difficult situations.

vocabulary.meaning_en: most important or most successful
vocabulary.example: We want to be the leading company in our field.

vocabulary.meaning_en: achieving good results
vocabulary.example: Our new product was very successful.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to admit you were wrong, even if it is difficult
vocabulary.example: He swallowed his pride and said sorry to his colleague.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to agree that something bad is true, e.g. that you were wrong
vocabulary.example: She admitted that she made a mistake.

vocabulary.meaning_en: in an angry, offended mood
vocabulary.example: He left the meeting in a huff.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to leave a place quickly and angrily
vocabulary.example: He stormed out of the office.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (of a phone or machine) not on
vocabulary.example: His phone is switched off.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to go towards a place
vocabulary.example: He was heading for the airport.

vocabulary.meaning_en: very angry
vocabulary.example: He left in a rage.

vocabulary.meaning_en: work is not the most important thing right now
vocabulary.example: My family needs me - work can wait.

fine_lines.title: advertise vs advertisement vs advert
fine_lines.explanation_ar: advertise فعل (يُعلن). advertisement اسم (إعلان). advert اختصار بريطاني لـ advertisement، وفي الأمريكية يقولون ad.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Advertise is the verb. Advertisement is the noun. Advert is the short British form; Americans say ad.

examples.sentence: We'll advertise the job next week.
I saw an advertisement for a sales job.
Did you see our advert in the newspaper?

fine_lines.title: keen to vs keen on
fine_lines.explanation_ar: keen to + فعل في المصدر: يريد بشدة أن يفعل (I'm keen to hear your ideas). keen on + اسم أو ing: يحب الشيء أو مهتم به (I'm keen on sales).
fine_lines.explanation_en: Keen to + base verb = want very much to do something. Keen on + noun/-ing = like or be interested in something.

examples.sentence: I'm keen to hear your ideas.
She's keen on learning new software.

expressions.phrase: I'll be advertising for a replacement for Tom today.
expressions.meaning_ar: سأنشر اليوم إعلانًا للبحث عن بديل لتوم.
expressions.meaning_en: Today I will advertise the job to find someone new.
expressions.example: I'll be advertising for a replacement for Sara this week.

expressions.phrase: I want to make some changes in the office.
expressions.meaning_ar: أريد أن أُجري بعض التغييرات في المكتب.
expressions.meaning_en: I plan to change some things at work.
expressions.example: As the new manager, I want to make some changes in the office.

expressions.phrase: I need to turn this business round.
expressions.meaning_ar: أحتاج إلى النهوض بهذه الشركة من جديد.
expressions.meaning_en: I must make this business successful again.
expressions.example: Sales are falling. I need to turn this business round.

expressions.phrase: I'm keen to hear your ideas.
expressions.meaning_en: I really want to hear what you think.
expressions.example: Please speak freely - I'm keen to hear your ideas.

expressions.phrase: Could we gather round for a quick meeting, please?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل يمكننا التجمّع لاجتماع قصير من فضلكم؟
expressions.meaning_en: A polite way to start a short meeting.
expressions.example: Excuse me, everyone. Could we gather round for a quick meeting, please?

expressions.phrase: It's time to get down to business.
expressions.meaning_ar: حان وقت البدء في العمل بجدية.
expressions.meaning_en: Let's start the real work now.
expressions.example: Coffee is finished - it's time to get down to business.

expressions.phrase: It's time to swallow your pride.
expressions.meaning_ar: حان الوقت لأن تتنازل عن كبريائك وتعترف بخطئك.
expressions.example: You made a mistake. It's time to swallow your pride and say sorry.

grammar.title: Future continuous: I'll be + verb-ing
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم will be + الفعل مع ing للحديث عن عمل سيكون جاريًا في وقت ما في المستقبل، أو عن خطة عادية مقررة. وهي تبدو ألطف وأكثر رسمية في إعلانات العمل: I'll be advertising for a replacement today.
grammar.explanation_en: Use will be + verb-ing for an action that will be in progress in the future, or for a planned, routine future action. It sounds smooth and professional: I'll be advertising for a replacement today.
examples: I'll be advertising the job today.
We'll be meeting the clients at ten.
She'll be working from home tomorrow.

grammar.title: Stating intentions: I want to / I need to / I'm keen to + verb
grammar.explanation_ar: عندما يعلن المدير خططه يستخدم: I want to (أريد)، I need to (يجب عليّ)، I'm keen to (أنا حريص على) + الفعل في المصدر.
grammar.explanation_en: A manager states plans with: I want to (wish), I need to (must), I'm keen to (really want) + base verb.
examples: I want to make some changes.
I need to turn this business round.
I'm keen to hear your ideas.

questions.explanation_ar: get down to business تعني البدء بالعمل بجدية.

questions.question: I'll be ___ for a replacement for Tom today.
'Turn this business round' means…
questions.explanation_ar: turn round هنا تعني النهوض بالشركة من جديد.
questions.explanation_en: It means make the business successful again.

questions.question: What phrase means to admit you are wrong?
questions.explanation_ar: swallow your pride أي الاعتراف بالخطأ رغم صعوبته.
questions.explanation_en: 'Swallow your pride' means admit you were wrong.

questions.question: A 'replacement' is…
choices: a person who takes someone else's place
questions.explanation_en: A replacement takes the place of another person.

questions.question: Tom left the office quickly and angrily. He…
Anna's phone call fails because Tom's phone is…

choices: I'm keen to hear your ideas.
questions.explanation_ar: I'm keen to hear your ideas دعوة لطيفة لمشاركة الأفكار.
questions.explanation_en: It shows you want to hear their ideas.
